core_concepts: classification; boundary making/unmaking; unequal participation; crossing and redefinition
questions_for_data: Which difference became consequential; who named it; what participation consequence followed; how was it crossed or avoided?
data_match: Strong for language speed, local knowledge, free grouping and invitations; weak for presumed ethnic boundaries without an event
blind_spots: May understate ordinary transfer, task and personality explanations
mechanical_application_risk: Coding every language, platform or background difference as cultural boundary

core_concepts: membership; acceptance; participation opportunity; trusted/confiding relation; help access
unit_of_analysis: distinct belonging dimension within a time-bounded school context
questions_for_data: Can membership coexist with exclusion, limited intimacy or restricted participation?
data_match: Strong: five survey items plus contrasting linked accounts
blind_spots: Does not by itself explain how relations or rules were produced
mechanical_application_risk: Collapsing belonging, exclusion, friendship, help and wellbeing into one endpoint

core_concepts: rule discovery; evaluation conventions; tacit participation norms; rule explainers
unit_of_analysis: task episode, rule interface and explanation event
questions_for_data: How were assignment, assessment, speaking, grouping and preparation expectations discovered; who explained them?
data_match: Strong for questionnaire task items and concrete oral-task/groupwork accounts; uneven for truly tacit rules
blind_spots: Can mislabel explicit school rules or workload as hidden curriculum
mechanical_application_risk: Calling every unfamiliar or strict practice hidden curriculum

core_concepts: good-student meaning; competence attribution; recognized/devalued resources; future-oriented self
unit_of_analysis: participant self-description tied to an academic episode
questions_for_data: When was rule unfamiliarity separated from ability; how were prior strengths translated or revalued?
data_match: Strong for Q5.2/Q5.3 and all three interviews, but retrospective and interviewer-framed
blind_spots: May psychologize institutional constraints or infer stable identity change
mechanical_application_risk: Treating confidence, grades or current habits as a single transformed identity

questions_for_data: Who explained or connected whom; was it voluntary; what benefit or pressure was reported?
data_match: Moderate in survey; only limited concrete interview actions
blind_spots: Network position and role identity are not observed directly
mechanical_application_risk: Equating bilingualism, mixed networks or one explanation with stable brokerage

core_concepts: relational medium choice; repertoire; audience/function differentiation; coexistence
questions_for_data: Which tools were retained, adopted or differentiated for old ties, school information and audiences?
data_match: Moderate in paired survey items; interview mechanism evidence is silent
blind_spots: Cannot establish actual communication sequence or platform effects
mechanical_application_risk: Reading platform names as identity, culture or integration indicators

core_concepts: emotional, informational, companionship and access functions; bonding/bridging distinction
questions_for_data: What did a tie provide; did it open opportunities, explain rules or sustain old relations?
data_match: Strong for Q5.4/Q5.5 and linked peer-support episodes
blind_spots: No complete network or resource-flow data; social capital accumulation is not measured
mechanical_application_risk: Ranking bridging as superior or inferring capital from group background

core_concepts: school, classroom, family, language regime, grade and resource layers
unit_of_analysis: event nested within classroom, school, family and migration context
questions_for_data: Could school type, language, grade, family resources or class organization better explain the event?
data_match: Strong as a rival-explanation framework; sparse case metadata prevent comparison of context effects
blind_spots: Broad context lists can become unfalsifiable
mechanical_application_risk: Calling a contextual condition an independent school or family effect

core_concepts: retrospective stages; turning points; accumulation; path dependence; reconfiguration
unit_of_analysis: participant-narrated sequence across pre-entry, initial, later and current periods
questions_for_data: Which events preceded another; which account indicates gradual change, re-selection or post-exit reconfiguration?
data_match: Moderate: time-bounded survey plus retrospective narratives, but no longitudinal observation
blind_spots: Recall compression and outcome-aware narration obscure ordering
mechanical_application_risk: Writing recalled sequences as observed development or causal trajectories

core_concepts: multiple identifications; context of reception; non-exclusive practices; situation dependence
unit_of_analysis: identity claim or practice in a specified audience/context
questions_for_data: Do practices and identifications vary by setting without requiring a fixed type?
data_match: Moderate for Q4 and cross-context self-descriptions; direct identity interviewing is uneven
blind_spots: Can import national categories as homogeneous cultures
mechanical_application_risk: Forcing assimilation/integration types or treating dual identity as universally optimal

core_concepts: situated choice; constrained action; opportunity structure; resource-dependent strategy
unit_of_analysis: action within a documented constraint and opportunity set
questions_for_data: What could the student do; what was enabled or constrained by grouping, peers, family resources and school rules?
data_match: Strong across linked cases and survey support items, but cannot estimate structural effects
blind_spots: Agency and structure can become catch-all labels
mechanical_application_risk: Celebrating adaptation strategies while individualizing exclusion or resource inequality

core_concepts: structural bridging position; enacted brokerage; brokerage identity
unit_of_analysis: network position, concrete act and self/other role attribution kept separate
questions_for_data: Is there network evidence, an actual connecting action, or only an assumed intermediary label?
data_match: Weak: network category and a few actions exist, but no network mapping or positional measures
blind_spots: Cannot identify bridging centrality, durable role or returns
mechanical_application_risk: Using mixed friendship circles as proof of brokering or social capital
